core_obligations: Reduce to a finite subset of A (proof lines 921-931): let Y = Spec(B) with closed point set Y_0 and let f : Y -> X be the given morphism; since A_w is the colimit of the A_E and the closed points of Spec(A_w) form the limit of the closed subsets Z_E, it suffices to produce a unique factorization A -> A_E -> B such that Y -> X_E maps Y_0 into Z_E.

Decompose Y into pieces (proof lines 931-940): the construction map Z_E -> X is bijective and the strata Z(E',E'') are constructible, so the preimages of the strata cut Y_0 into open and closed pieces; since Y_0 is the set of connected components of Y, this gives a corresponding decomposition of Y into open and closed pieces, reducing the problem to the case f(Y_0) contained in one stratum Z(E',E'') for a decomposition E = E' disjoint union E''.

Conclude in the stratum case (proof lines 940-945): in that case f(Y) is contained in the set of points specializing to Z(E',E''), which is homeomorphic to X_{E',E''}, so there is a unique continuous map Y -> X_{E',E''} over X, and by the faithfulness statement this comes from a unique morphism of schemes, giving the required unique factorization.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the universal property to a factorization through one of the partial w-localizations.
Cut the closed points of Y into the constructible pieces determined by the strata and reduce to a single stratum.
Convert the unique continuous map on the stratum into a unique morphism of schemes.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the universal property of the w-localization: for any ring map A -> B with Spec(B) w-local there is a unique factorization A -> A_w -> B such that Spec(B) -> Spec(A_w) is w-local (statement lines 913-919). The proof (proof lines 921-946) reduces to a factorization through a partial w-localization, cuts the closed points of the target into the constructible strata, and converts the resulting unique continuous map into a unique morphism of schemes. H2: a three-step reduction with three inputs, written out in full.
